issues.description: Method name inconsistency: the example usage in template Main.java calls farm.feed(), but the problem statement and the solution implementation define and describe feedAllAnimals(). The PROBLEM_STATEMENT (lines 108-111) instructs implementing Farm.feedAllAnimals(); the SOLUTION_REPOSITORY Farm.java defines public void feedAllAnimals() (line 27); the TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY Main.java example instead calls farm.feed() (line 20). This naming mismatch can confuse students about which method to implement and will cause the example code to not compile if they follow the template example.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the example in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java consistent with the UML/problem statement and solution. Replace the call to farm.feed() with farm.feedAllAnimals() (or alternatively, if feed() was intended, update the problem statement and solution to define a feed() method). Prefer updating Main.java to call farm.feedAllAnimals() to match the UML and specification.

issues.description: The concept 'feed all animals on the farm' is referred to by different identifiers: the problem statement and solution use the method name feedAllAnimals(), while the template's example code in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java calls farm.feed(). A student reading the example may look for a feed() method in the Farm class (which does not exist in the template or solution) and become confused about which API to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template consistent with the specification and solution by changing the example call in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java from farm.feed() to farm.feedAllAnimals(). Alternatively (less preferred), add a small delegating method public void feed() in Farm that simply calls feedAllAnimals(), and document it; prefer updating the example to feedAllAnimals() to match the problem statement and solution code.
